title: Day Trader Salary: How to Convert Hourly Rates to Annual Pay Including Casual Loading and Super
description: Understand day trader salary calculations: convert hourly rates to annual pay using 38-hour weeks, casual loading, and super paid on top. Fair Work rates and tax explained.
salarySummary: For a casual day trader on the National Minimum Wage, the annual gross pay including 25% casual loading is about $65,300, with super of around $7,800 paid on top.

faqs.q: What is the day trader salary for a casual worker on the National Minimum Wage?
faqs.a: A casual day trader aged 21 or over who is award-free must be paid at least the National Minimum Wage plus 25% casual loading. From 1 July 2026, that is $33.05 per hour. Working 38 hours per week for 52 weeks gives an annual gross of about $65,300. Superannuation of 12% is paid on top of ordinary earnings, adding roughly $7,800, but note the maximum contribution base of $270,830 may limit super on higher earnings.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated for a day trader salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is 12% of ordinary time earnings, paid by the employer on top of the base salary. For a casual day trader, ordinary earnings include the casual loading. The super guarantee applies up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year (2026–27). For example, on a $65,300 annual salary, super would be about $7,836. This amount is not deducted from the employee's pay; it is an additional cost to the employer.

faqs.q: What tax applies to a day trader salary in 2026–27?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, Australian resident tax rates are: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000, 30% from $45,001 to $135,000, 37% from $135,001 to $190,000, and 45% above $190,000. A 2% Medicare levy generally applies. For a day trader earning $65,300, the tax would be approximately $11,067 plus Medicare levy of $1,306, leaving take-home pay of about $52,927 before any offsets or deductions.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Your Day Trader Salary

Whether you are a self-employed day trader or considering a role that pays by the hour, converting an hourly rate to an annual salary helps you compare job offers and plan your finances. In Australia, the standard full-time working week is 38 hours, and most calculations use that figure. For casual workers, a 25% loading is added to the base rate, and superannuation is paid on top. This guide explains how to calculate your day trader salary using the latest Fair Work and ATO figures.

### The Basic Formula

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks.

If you are a permanent employee, your hourly rate is your base rate. If you are casual, you receive the base rate plus 25% casual loading. The Fair Work Ombudsman states that the casual loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When you use [the timesheet](/), you can enter your base hourly rate and check a box to add the casual loading. Never enter a rate that already includes the loading.

For example, the National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for a full-time adult employee. A casual worker doing the same job gets $33.05 per hour ($26.44 × 1.25). Working 38 hours each week for 52 weeks gives:

- Annual gross (casual) = $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,306.80
- Superannuation (12% on top) = $7,836.82
- Total cost to employer = $73,143.62

This is your day trader salary before tax. The same formula works for any hourly rate, whether you are covered by an award or an enterprise agreement.

### National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage applies to employees not covered by an award or agreement. Most workers are covered by a modern award, which sets higher minimum rates for specific industries and roles. You can find the correct pay guide for your award on the [pay guides](/blog) page. The Fair Work Commission reviews these rates each year. From 1 July 2026, the national minimum wage is $26.44 per hour, but award rates may be higher.

For a day trader salary, if you are self-employed, you do not have a minimum wage – you set your own rates. However, if you hire employees, you must pay at least the relevant minimum.

### Casual Loading and Super Paid on Top

Casual loading of 25% is added to the base hourly rate. This is not a bonus; it replaces entitlements like annual leave and sick leave. Superannuation is calculated on ordinary time earnings, which includes the casual loading. The super guarantee rate is 12% for 2026–27, and it is paid by the employer on top of the salary. The maximum contribution base is $270,830 per year – earnings above that do not attract compulsory super.

When you use [the timesheet](/), you can see the effect of casual loading and super on your annual figures. Remember that super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost for the employer.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross, multiply your weekly pay by two. For the casual day trader earning $33.05 per hour:

- Weekly gross = $33.05 × 38 = $1,255.90
- Fortnightly gross = $1,255.90 × 2 = $2,511.80

This can help you budget and compare with salaried roles that pay monthly.

### Tax on Your Day Trader Salary

For 2026–27, the Australian Tax Office uses these resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37% on excess over $135,000
- Over $190,000: 45% on excess over $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% applies to most taxpayers. For a day trader salary of $65,306.80, the tax would be approximately:

- Tax on first $18,200: $0
- Tax on $18,201 to $45,000: ($45,000 – $18,200) × 15% = $4,020
- Tax on $45,001 to $65,306.80: ($65,306.80 – $45,000) × 30% = $6,092.04
- Total tax: $10,112.04
- Medicare levy (2% of $65,306.80): $1,306.14
- Total deductions: $11,418.18
- Take-home pay: $53,888.62

This is an estimate. It does not include the Medicare levy surcharge, HELP repayments, or tax offsets. For a precise calculation, use the ATO's tax estimator.

### Using the Timesheet for Your Day Trader Salary

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate and toggle casual loading. It shows your annual gross, fortnightly pay, estimated tax, Medicare, and super. You can adjust hours per week if you work less than 38 hours. The tool assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, capped at the maximum contribution base.

### Summary

Your day trader salary depends on your hourly rate, whether you are casual or permanent, and the number of hours you work. Use the formula hourly × hours per week × 52 to get annual gross. Add 25% for casual loading if applicable. Super is paid on top at 12%. Tax is calculated on the gross amount using the progressive scale. For award-covered employees, check the relevant pay guide for minimum rates. The [reference tables](/data) page has historical rates and more details.
